title: Why Does Alaska Belong to the US?
art_style: cute 2D vector sticker illustration, minimalist flat design, chibi proportions, flat colors with no gradients, muted earthy palette, clean dark outline, full body, centered, isolated on a solid plain white background, no text

scenes.narration: Alaska is part of the United States. But it used to belong to Russia.
In 1867, the US bought it from Russia for seven point two million dollars.
scenes.tts: In eighteen sixty-seven, the US bought it from Russia for seven point two million dollars.

scenes.narration: That works out to about two cents an acre, for a piece of land the size of a small continent.
Why would Russia sell? It was far away, hard to defend, and Russia needed money after losing the Crimean War.
Russia also feared that Britain, right next door in Canada, would simply take it in the next war.
In America, people laughed. They called it Seward's Folly, after the man who made the deal.
But look how big it really is.
Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas, and bigger than California, Texas and Montana combined.
Then the joke turned around. Gold was found in the 1890s, and people rushed north.
scenes.tts: Then the joke turned around. Gold was found in the eighteen-nineties, and people rushed north.

scenes.narration: And in 1968, they found the biggest oil field in North America, at Prudhoe Bay.
scenes.tts: And in nineteen sixty-eight, they found the biggest oil field in North America, at Prudhoe Bay.

scenes.narration: Seven million dollars turned out to be one of the best real estate deals in history, and Russia never got it back.
Should Russia have sold Alaska? Yes or no?
